column1: Wait your turn. It's just like at the bank. (Other people want to make their deposits first.)
column2: 排隊等等吧，這就跟銀行一樣。（人家也想先進去「辦點事」呢。）

column1: You can't reach the outhouse from up here.
column2: 你從這裡構不到茅房。

column1: The outhouse door has a signature half-moon cutout.
column2: 茅房門上有個招牌半月形鏤空。

column1: (STAR TREK) The engines are already at maximum reverse thrust, Captain! They're givin' it all they've got!
column2: （星艦迷航記）「引擎已經全速反推到底了，艦長！它們已經卯足全力啦！」

column1: You haven't seen a line this long here since Mom served her famous Chicken Sushi w/Egg Tartare.
column2: 自從老媽端出她那道著名的「雞肉壽司佐韃靼蛋醬」以來，這裡就沒排過這麼長的隊了。

column1: Hey, you guys! You feel okay?
column2: 喂，各位！你們還好吧？

column1: The only response is a chorus of churning stomachs, roiling bowels, and floodgates straining to open.
column2: 回應你的只有此起彼落的腸鳴、翻攪的腹部，還有拼命想開閘的水門。

column1: |c2|"Hey, buddy, no cutting!"|c|
column2: |c2|「喂，老兄，不准插隊！」|c|

column1: |c3|"It's people like you that give people like you a bad name!"|c|
column2: |c3|「就是你這種人，讓你這種人名聲都臭掉了！」|c|

column1: A few moments later, you emerge feeling refreshed.
column2: 過了一會兒，你神清氣爽地走了出來。

column1: Gee! That water's got a nasty kick to it.
column2: 哇！這水後座力還真不小。

column1: Don't touch him, Captain! He's liable to blow any second!
column2: 別碰他，艦長！他隨時都會爆炸！

column1: He's really gotta go.
column2: 他真的憋不住了。

column1: Don't talk to him, he's concentrating.
column2: 別跟他說話，他正在集中精神。

column1: (SCOTTY OF STAR TREK) I canna tell how much more she kin take, Captain!
column2: （星艦迷航記的史考特）「俺說不準她還能撐多久啊，艦長！」

column1: How long can she wait? Not long, if she keeps bouncing like that!
column2: 她還能撐多久？照這樣一直扭來扭去，看來撐不了多久！

column1: She can't hear you over the mighty roar of her lower gastro-intestinal tract.
column2: 她下腹那雷鳴般的腸胃巨響，蓋過了你說的話，她根本聽不見。

column1: (SCOTTY) He's gonna explode, Captain, and neither you or I or anyone in the Universe can stop it!
column2: （史考特）「他就要爆炸了，艦長，這事兒不管是你、是俺，還是全宇宙誰都攔不住！」

column1: This one appears to be practicing the Jitterbug.
column2: 這位看起來正在練搖擺舞。

column1: Say! Do any of you guys know how to Madison?
column2: 喂！你們哪個會跳麥迪遜舞步啊？

column1: Nobody's laughing.
column2: 沒有人笑。

column1: Boi-oi-oing! That one hit a 9.0 on the Free Plug-O-Meter!
column2: 咚啊咚啊咚！那個在「置入式廣告指數」上飆到 9.0 分！

column1: Plug-O-Meter
column2: 置入式廣告指數

column1: That pulley never worked right in the first place. It's not going to work for you now.
column2: 那個滑輪打從一開始就沒好用過，現在也不會突然聽你的話。

column1: A block-and-tackle was erected here for unloading wagons. Unfortunately, it couldn't block and tackle at the same time.
column2: 這裡架了一組滑輪吊索，是用來卸貨的。可惜它沒辦法一邊「擋」一邊「拉」。

column1: As you reach the top of the water tower, the crowd cheers!
column2: 你爬上水塔頂端的那一刻，群眾歡聲雷動！

column1: |c2|"Thank God, It's Freddy!"|c|
column2: |c2|「謝天謝地，是佛萊迪！」|c|

column1: |c3|"We're number one! We're number one!"|c|
column2: |c3|「我們是第一！我們是第一！」|c|

column1: |c0|"What are you going to do now, Freddy?"|c|
column2: |c0|「你接下來打算怎麼辦，佛萊迪？」|c|

column1: I'm going to SierraLand!
column2: 我要去雪樂樂園！

column1: You reached the top. Too bad nobody was here to applaud your achievement!
column2: 你爬到頂了。可惜沒人在這裡替你鼓掌喝采！

column1: The bluff stays put, no matter how hard you tug.
column2: 不管你怎麼拉，那片峭壁都紋風不動。

column1: This is the eastern portion of Bluff Street, so-named for scenic Collier Bluff.
column2: 這是峭壁街的東段，因風景優美的柯里爾峭壁而得名。

column1: Didn't anyone warn you about digging near an outhouse?
column2: 都沒人警告過你，別在茅房附近亂挖嗎？

column1: You're tongue-tied.
column2: 你舌頭打結了，說不出話。

column1: You can't reach the rope from here!
column2: 你從這裡構不到那條繩子！

column1: The lasso dangles from the top of the water tower.
column2: 套索垂掛在水塔頂端。

column1: Your snare the tower top! The crowd eats it up!
column2: 你套住了塔頂！群眾看得如癡如醉！

column1: |c3|"Who's the shmuck with the rope?"|c|
column2: |c3|「拿繩子的那個傻蛋是誰啊？」|c|

column1: |c2|"Be careful you don't put an eye out!"|c|
column2: |c2|「小心別把自己眼睛戳瞎了！」|c|

column1: Hot dog, you roped the top of the water tower! What a shame there's no audience to appreciate your deed.
column2: 太厲害了，你套中水塔頂端了！可惜沒有觀眾能欣賞你這番壯舉。

column1: You wash your hands. (A feeling wholly unfamiliar to you!)
column2: 你洗了手。（這種感覺你可完全不熟悉！）

column1: You don't need any water right now!
column2: 你現在不需要水！

column1: You carefully fill one of your empty beer bottles with water from the tower.
column2: 你小心翼翼地用塔裡的水，把一個空啤酒瓶裝滿。

column1: You don't need any water at the moment.
column2: 你目前不需要水。

column1: One bottle full of water is enough.
column2: 一瓶水就夠了。

column1: You can't do that from up here!
column2: 你在這麼高的地方沒辦法這麼做！

column1: Water's running from the spigot.
column2: 水龍頭正在流水。

column1: The water just babbles.
column2: 水只是潺潺地流著。

column1: You don't need to fill the whisky glass with water. (Besides, some folks in town would consider it sacrilegious!)
column2: 你不需要把威士忌杯裝滿水。（再說，鎮上有些人會覺得這根本是褻瀆！）

column1: Trying to make the World's Largest Fizzy?
column2: 想調出全世界最大杯的氣泡飲嗎？

column1: The Deflatulizer is for the horses only. That's the water supply for the whole town!
column2: 除脹氣機是專門給馬用的。那邊可是全鎮的水源！

column1: You can't reach the water tank hatch from down here.
column2: 你從這麼下面構不到水塔的艙口。

column1: There's a small hatch on top of the water tank.
column2: 水塔頂端有個小艙口。

column1: That would taint the town's water supply!
column2: 那樣會污染全鎮的水源！

column1: Watered-down beer for the whole town? That's Sam Andreas's job!
column2: 讓全鎮喝到摻水的啤酒？那是山姆·安德列斯的活兒！

column1: You can't pour the purification solution into the water tank from down here.
column2: 你從這麼下面沒辦法把淨化液倒進水塔裡。

column1: Open the hatch first instead of pouring the purification solution on the roof of the water tank!
column2: 先把艙口打開，別把淨化液直接倒在水塔屋頂上！

column1: You carefully pour the purification solution into the town's water supply. Excellent job!
column2: 你小心地把淨化液倒進了全鎮的水源裡。幹得漂亮！

column1: It warn't more 'n a few hours, the folks of Coarsegold wuz feelin' a whole heckuva lot better, their bowels all settled down and happy. Freddy knew he could relax now; ever'thing was calm 'n' peaceful. But round 'bout midnight that very same night, trouble struck again. Freddy was in his own bed, sound asleep, when...
column2: 不消幾個時辰，粗金鎮的鄉親們都覺得舒坦多了，一個個腸胃安穩、心滿意足。佛萊迪心想這下總算能鬆口氣了，一切歸於平靜安寧。誰知就在當天半夜，麻煩又找上門來。佛萊迪正在自己床上睡得香甜，這時……

column1: Hello in there!
column2: 裡面有人嗎！

column1: (FUNNY VOICE) "There's nobody in here but us E. Coli!"
column2: （搞笑怪聲）「這裡只有咱們大腸桿菌，沒別人啦！」

column1: You can't seem to get a good grip on the shingles.
column2: 你怎麼樣都抓不牢那些屋瓦。

column1: You can't reach the roof of the water tank from here.
column2: 你從這裡構不到水塔的屋頂。

column1: The shingled roof of the water tank protects the entire water supply of the village of Coarsegold from dust, dirt, and bird droppings.
column2: 水塔那鋪著木瓦的屋頂，替粗金鎮全村的水源擋住了灰塵、髒污和鳥糞。

column1: The building's closed. There's no use milling around here.
column2: 這棟建築已經打烊了，你在這兒磨蹭也沒用。

column1: It's the Old Grist Mill. Since Mr. Grist left town, not much happens there.
column2: 這是老磨坊。自從葛里斯特先生離開小鎮後，這裡就沒什麼動靜了。

column1: The metal top of the tower is held very firmly in place. No amount of pulling could possibly budge it.
column2: 塔頂的金屬蓋固定得非常牢，你怎麼拉都休想撼動分毫。

column1: Your lasso isn't quite long enough to reach the top of the water tank from down here.
column2: 你的套索長度不夠，從這麼下面構不到水塔頂端。

column1: Using the lasso, you manage to climb up to the tippy-top of the tower.
column2: 你靠著套索，總算爬上了塔的最頂端。

column1: A short strong metal pole projects from the roof of the water tank.
column2: 水塔屋頂上突出一根短而堅固的金屬桿。

column1: Remembering your father's advice about never using the topmost rungs of a ladder, you stop just short of the ladder top.
column2: 想起老爸交代過絕不能踩梯子最頂那幾階，你便在快到頂端前停了下來。

column1: You can't reach the ladder from up here.
column2: 你在這麼高的地方構不到梯子。

column1: You can't seem to pick up the ladder right now. It suddenly seems so much heavier, for some strange reason!
column2: 你現在好像搬不動這梯子。不知道為什麼，它突然重了好多！

column1: The ladder is propped up against the side of the water tower tank.
column2: 梯子靠在水塔塔身的一側。

column1: You'll have to climb back down the rope first.
column2: 你得先順著繩子爬下去才行。

column1: It's wood, what more did you need to know?
column2: 就是木頭做的，你還想知道什麼？

column1: The ladder doesn't quite reach far enough.
column2: 這梯子的長度還不夠遠。

column1: You can't get a good throw while standing on the ladder.
column2: 你站在梯子上沒辦法好好瞄準投擲。

column1: (BONES LIKE) Dammit, Jim, you're a Pharmacist, not a cattle rustler!
column2: （模仿骨頭的口吻）「該死，吉姆，你是個藥劑師，不是偷牛賊！」

column1: This tank stores the whole town's drinking water supply.
column2: 這座水塔裝著全鎮的飲用水。

column1: There's nothing inside or outside the wagon worth taking.
column2: 這輛篷車裡裡外外都沒什麼值得拿的東西。

column1: By the side of the road sits an old covered wagon. (It's covered for theft and fire.)
column2: 路邊停著一輛老舊的篷車。（篷布嘛，就當它「有保」防盜防火險吧。）

column1: The tower is falling apart. You can't get to the top of it safely.
column2: 這座塔搖搖欲墜，你沒辦法安全爬到頂端。

column1: A creaking old windmill tower, haphazardly assembled from now-rotting timbers, graces the beautiful Coarsegold skyline.
column2: 一座嘎吱作響的老舊風車塔，用一堆早已腐朽的木料東拼西湊搭成，為粗金鎮美麗的天際線增色不少。

column1: Have you ever had your hand sliced off by a propeller? Would you LIKE to? Then don't try sticking your hand in the windmill blades!
column2: 你有被螺旋槳削掉手的經驗嗎？你會想要嗎？那就別把手伸進風車葉片裡！

column1: Now THAT's the pot calling the kettle black!
column2: 這下可真是五十步笑百步了！

column1: Ye Olde 'Orehouse usually isn't open during the day. Wait until dark, cowboy!
column2: 「金屋藏嬌樓」白天通常不營業，牛仔，等天黑了再來吧！

column1: That's the door to the brothel.
column2: 那是妓院的門。

column1: Freddy! Your store is ready to burn. You must save your town from sure destruction!
column2: 佛萊迪！你的店就快燒起來了。你得拯救全鎮，別讓它毀於一旦！

column1: The boss is more than a little upset. Seems that our "friend" has been thwarting every plan so far.
column2: 老大可不只是有點不高興而已。看來咱們那位「朋友」，到目前為止把每個計畫都搞砸了。

column1: Yep. Sumpin's gots to be done about it.
column2: 沒錯，這事兒非得處理不可。

column1: Absolutely. Now let's get down to business. What is the best way to get rid of our little problem -- PERMANENTLY?
column2: 一點沒錯。那咱們就開門見山吧，要怎麼樣才能徹底、永久地解決掉這個小麻煩？

column1: How 'bout hanging?
column2: 吊死他怎麼樣？

column1: No. Too quick and merciless. Poison?
column2: 不行，太快也太乾脆了。下毒呢？

column1: Nah. Too unsure. Ancient Egyptian dagger?
column2: 不行，太不保險了。古埃及匕首呢？

column1: I can't find mine. Got one on ya?
column2: 俺那把找不到了，你身上有帶嗎？

column1: Not at the moment. It don't matter how we do it, s'long as we do it soon. And we don't want no proof it was us, neither, and nuttin' to connect it to da Boss.
column2: 現在沒有。怎麼下手不重要，反正得快點動手。而且咱們不能留下任何證據，更不能讓人查到跟老大有關。

column1: Excellent thought. And the Boss has arranged for a bit of muscle to come on in and make sure the entire town's cleaned out PDQ. We'll be rid of that do-gooder and all his flea-bitten friends in no time! Ha, ha!
column2: 這主意妙。老大已經安排好幾個打手進來，保證把整個鎮子麻溜地清乾淨。咱們很快就能擺脫那個多管閒事的傢伙和他那票邋遢朋友了！哈哈！

column1: (CRUEL LAUGH) Bwah, hah hah!
column2: （奸笑）「哇哈，哈哈哈！」

column1: Laughing cruelly, they sit back to reflect on their villainy.
column2: 兩人奸笑著往後一靠，細細回味自己的惡行。

column1: It's P. H. Balance, the town banker, relaxing on the brothel porch with a good cigar. The thought of him "conversing" with one of Madame's nubile young professionals is enough to make you swear off banking forever.
column2: 是鎮上的銀行家P·H·貝倫斯，正叼著上等雪茄，在妓院門廊上悠哉休息。一想到他跟歐薇莉夫人手下哪位年輕「專業人士」「交流意見」，你就恨不得從此再也不跟銀行打交道。

column1: Am I interrupting anything?
column2: 我打擾到你們了嗎？

column1: OH! Er... why, of course not, Mr. Pharkas, we were just talking about y...UGH!
column2: 噢！呃……當然沒有啊，法卡斯先生，我們正在談你……唔！

column1: What he means is, we were simply chatting after an invigorating, ah, workout.
column2: 他的意思是，我們只是在一番，呃，提振精神的「運動」過後閒聊幾句。

column1: Did I hear you fellas say something about getting rid of somebody?
column2: 我剛剛是不是聽到你們在講要「解決掉」什麼人？

column1: No.
column2: 沒有。

column1: Yes.
column2: 有。

column1: Rats. Err, we were talking about getting rid of rats. Rats at the Bank, terrible problem. Sheriff Shift was telling me ways to eradicate the vermin.
column2: 老鼠。呃，我們在講怎麼除掉老鼠。銀行裡鬧老鼠，麻煩得很。席夫特警長正在跟我說怎麼滅這些害蟲。

column1: (SOTTO VOCE) |c1|You're the only rat at the bank.|c|
column2: （壓低聲音）|c1|銀行裡唯一的老鼠就是你。|c|

column1: I'm sorry, what was that?
column2: 不好意思，你說什麼？

column1: I said, "If only you had a cat at the bank."
column2: 我是說：「銀行裡要是有隻貓就好了。」

column1: Oh. Yes, I suppose that would work.
column2: 噢，對啊，我想那應該有用。

column1: Well, I'll leave you gentlemen to continue your conversation.
column2: 好啦，我就不打擾兩位先生繼續聊了。

column1: They snicker softly to themselves.
column2: 他們兩人低聲竊笑起來。

column1: You briefly consider showing P. H. Balance what you think of him... with a knuckle sandwich! But if they were talking YOU, the Sheriff is just itching to get you out the way. A fight would give him all the provocation he needs. Discretion wins out over raw virile manliness.
column2: 你一度考慮讓P·H·貝倫斯嚐嚐你的「拳頭三明治」，好好表達一下對他的看法！但如果他們剛才是在講你，警長可正巴不得找藉口把你除掉。動手打架正好給他一個現成的理由。三思而後行，終究還是勝過逞一時血氣之勇。

column1: Now then, Frederick. Please don't disturb us anymore.
column2: 好了，佛萊德里克。請你別再打擾我們了。

column1: You can barely see a glint from the nitrous oxide canister.
column2: 你勉強能看到笑氣鋼瓶反射出的一點光。

column1: You take careful aim with your pistol and slowly squeeze off a shot.
column2: 你舉起手槍仔細瞄準，緩緩扣下扳機。

column1: You did it! You shot off the canister's valve.
column2: 你成功了！你把鋼瓶的閥門射了下來。

column1: Good idea, but you just don't have a straight shot from here.
column2: 這主意不錯，但你從這裡沒有直射的角度。

column1: Oh, no you don't! You can't shoot the canister the EASY way, from up close! Try it from far away, just like you'd HAVE to in real life!
column2: 喔，不行不行！你不能用近距離這種「簡單模式」射那個鋼瓶！得從遠處下手，就跟現實生活中你「必須」做到的一樣！

column1: Yiparooni, Freddy done made them cowhands laugh themselves to death with a well-placed bullet.
column2: 呀呼，佛萊迪靠著一發精準的子彈，把那些牛仔們笑到活活斷氣。

column1: It's too dark for you to make out any details of that thing hanging from the hotel balcony.
column2: 天色太暗了，你看不清楚旅館陽台上掛著的那個東西的細節。

column1: You can't see the hotel through the brothel. You left your X-Ray glasses at the Pharmacy!
column2: 你沒辦法隔著妓院看穿到旅館。你的X光眼鏡忘在藥局了！

column1: You can't reach the bunting from here.
column2: 你從這裡構不到那面彩旗。

column1: Good idea, but you missed!
column2: 主意不錯，可惜你沒射中！

column1: There's no longer any need to shoot the bunting.
column2: 現在已經沒必要再射那面彩旗了。

column1: Potshots at the hotel? From here? Save your ammo!
column2: 想從這裡朝旅館亂開槍？省點子彈吧！

column1: You can see the bunting on the Hotel balcony clear as day from here. The canister of nitrous oxide is sitting on the top rail, just minding its own business.
column2: 你從這裡可以把旅館陽台上的彩旗看得一清二楚。那瓶笑氣就擱在欄杆頂端，安安靜靜地待著。

column1: The bunting is clearly advertising Open Mike Night for comedians at Mom's Cafe. Now that the Hotel is out of business, Mom gets free advertising space!
column2: 那面彩旗上明明白白寫著「老媽餐館開放麥克風喜劇之夜」的廣告。既然旅館已經倒了，老媽正好白撿一塊免費廣告版面！

column1: You wanna touch that bunting from HERE? You must be thinking of that other Al Lowe game: PLASTIC MAN, FRONTIER PHARMACIST.
column2: 你想從「這裡」摸到那面彩旗？你該不會把這款遊戲跟艾爾·洛威的另一款作品搞混了吧：《塑膠人：邊疆藥劑師》。

column1: Unfortunately, you can't shoot from this complimentary close-up screen! You'll have to do it like a REAL man... from far away!
column2: 很遺憾，你不能從這個「附贈特寫畫面」開槍！你得像個真正的男子漢那樣……從遠處來。

column1: It's a pressurized metal canister of NO2, also known as Nitrous Oxide, alias "laughing gas."
column2: 這是一瓶加壓的NO2金屬鋼瓶，也就是一氧化二氮，別名「笑氣」。

column1: You can see it as plain as day, but you can't possibly reach it from here.
column2: 你能看得一清二楚，但從這裡根本不可能構得到。

column1: Sheriff Chicken P. Shift is sitting on Madame's front porch, smoking cigars with P.H. Balance, the village banker. A hint of coal oil drifts through the night air... from him! The thought of Shift and Balance messin' around with Madame's working girls makes you thankful you don't participate in any disease-tradin' activities!
column2: 警長切肯·P·席夫特正坐在夫人門廊上，跟村裡的銀行家P·H·貝倫斯一起抽著雪茄。夜色中飄來一絲煤油味……是從他身上傳來的！一想到席夫特和貝倫斯跟歐薇莉夫人手下姑娘們鬼混的畫面，你就慶幸自己沒摻和這種互通有無的「疾病交流活動」！

column1: Sheriff, you know about the fire down at the Assay Office?
column2: 警長，你知道驗金所那邊失火的事嗎？

column1: Fire?
column2: 火災？

column1: No!
column2: 沒有！

column1: Ya don't say!
column2: 不會吧！

column1: That's dreadful.
column2: 那可真是糟透了。

column1: Why, iffn ah'm not mistaken, a fire there could wipe out mosta Main Street! And take yer Pharmacy right up along with it! One hates to contemplate it! <chuckle>
column2: 哎呀，俺要是沒猜錯，那場火可能把大街給燒掉大半！連你那間藥局也一併陪葬！這事兒想都不敢想啊！<竊笑>

column1: <snort, giggle>
column2: <哼笑，竊笑>

column1: Fortunately, I put the fire out. Baking soda, you know.
column2: 幸好，我把火給撲滅了，用的是小蘇打粉。

column1: Yew WHAT?
column2: 你說啥？

column1: Put the fire OUT?
column2: 把火「撲滅」了？

column1: Whut'd yew go and do THET fer?
column2: 你幹嘛要去做那種事？

column1: Somebody could've gotten hurt! Surely you didn't want me to leave the fire BURNING, did you?
column2: 那樣可能會有人受傷的！你該不會希望我放著火燒下去吧？

column1: Sheriff Shift and Phineas exchange glances.
column2: 席夫特警長和菲尼斯互看了一眼。

column1: Well?
column2: 怎麼樣？

column1: 'Course not, Pharkwell. Yew done a good job there. We're right proud of yew.
column2: 那當然不是，法卡威。你這事兒辦得好，俺們可為你感到驕傲呢。

column1: Uh... yes, Frederick, very commendable.
column2: 呃……對，佛萊德里克，非常值得嘉許。

column1: Well, have a lovely evening, gentlemen.
column2: 好了，兩位先生，祝你們有個美好的夜晚。

column1: Yeah, whutever.
column2: 嗯，隨便啦。

column1: Same to you.
column2: 你也一樣。

column1: Figuring that you were the topic of the Sheriff's plotting, you have an irresistible urge to knock his block off. But the TRULY amazing thing is how you manage to RESIST that urge!
column2: 你猜到自己就是警長密謀的對象，忍不住升起一股想扁他的衝動。但真正厲害的是，你居然能忍住這股衝動！

column1: Hey, now! Don't bother us, Pharmore. We's tryin' to have a conversation here.
column2: 喂，法卡摩，別來煩俺們，俺們正在談事情呢。

column1: |c2|Ye Olde 'Ore House est. 1869 George Armstrong Custer Slept Here Repeatedly|c|
column2: |c2|金屋藏嬌樓　創立於1869年　喬治·阿姆斯壯·卡斯特將軍在此屢屢留宿|c|

column1: Leave Madame's sign alone. You wouldn't want her running off with the Pharmacy sign, would you?
column2: 別動夫人的招牌。你總不希望她把藥局的招牌也順手牽走吧？

column1: That's just one of the many dried-out, half-dead trees found in the area.
column2: 那不過是這一帶眾多枯萎、半死不活的樹之一。

column1: You have neither the desire nor the talent to climb trees.
column2: 你既沒有爬樹的意願，也沒有爬樹的天分。

column1: The curtains are flappin' lazily in the warm spring breeze, carrying the scent of... well, you don't wanna know.
column2: 窗簾在溫暖的春風中懶洋洋地飄動，還帶著一股……算了，你不會想知道的。

column1: You couldn't possibly reach those curtains from here. Besides, you don't know where those curtain have been!
column2: 你從這裡根本不可能構到那些窗簾。再說，你也不知道那些窗簾都經歷過什麼事！

column1: Looks like somebody's burning the midnight oil... or rubbing it!
column2: 看來有人正在挑燈夜戰……還是說在「揉」燈油呢！

column1: Located on this rocky hillside is Madame Ovaree's place of business, a custom-built bawdyhouse built in the fashion of the Pastel Gothics. Of course, they had to get the rocks off the property before they could build here.
column2: 這片多岩的山坡上，坐落著歐薇莉夫人的產業，一棟仿「柔彩哥德式」風格量身打造的風月場所。當然，蓋房子之前，他們得先把地上的石頭清乾淨才行。

column1: The wood on the outside of the brothel is chipped, rotting, and nearly useless. (In other words, it's nearly ex-siding!)
column2: 妓院外牆的木板缺角又腐爛，幾乎沒用了。（換句話說，這外牆已經「牆」途末路啦！）

column1: You can't see into the brothel from out here, but Madame does cater to Peeping Toms, and at a slight discount.
column2: 你從外面看不進妓院裡頭，不過夫人倒是有專門服務偷窺狂的項目，還打了點小折扣。

column1: You consider writing "Wash Me" with your finger in the dirt on the glass. However, Madame would never guess you meant the window!
column2: 你想著要不要用手指在玻璃上的灰塵寫「洗我」兩個字。不過，夫人大概怎麼也猜不到你指的是這扇窗戶吧！

column1: Madame had this gazebo built as part of her "Real Ol' Fashioned Romance Special," which cost an additional $1.25. It was never used. Coarsegold is filled with unromantic cheapskates.
column2: 夫人蓋了這座涼亭，是她「復古浪漫特別方案」的一部分，得另外加收1.25美元。結果從沒人用過。粗金鎮裡到處都是不解風情的小氣鬼。

column1: Fudd's First Law: If you push it hard enough, it will fall over.
column2: 「法德第一定律」：只要推得夠用力，什麼東西都會倒。

column1: It's a white picket fence, separating Madame's property from the Great Desert Valley to the south.
column2: 這是一道白色尖木柵欄，把夫人的地產和南邊的大沙漠谷地隔開。

column1: If you picket, it'll get worse.
column2: 你要是去抗議，情況只會更糟。

column1: It's a cactus, growing just beyond the fence.
column2: 這是一株仙人掌，長在柵欄外頭不遠處。

column1: Touch that cactus and you may get a little prick.
column2: 碰那株仙人掌，你可能會被扎一下，還可能碰上個「小刺頭」。

column1: Here on the "other side of the tracks," in the baddest part of town, stands Madame Sadie Ovaree's "Ye Olde 'Ore House," a gazebo, and a lot of foxtail, scrub, and brush. (Or "Scrub Brush," as Madame's fond of calling it.) You can also see parts of Main Street off in the distance.
column2: 在這「鐵軌另一頭」，也就是鎮上治安最差的地帶，坐落著莎蒂·歐薇莉夫人的「金屋藏嬌樓」、一座涼亭，還有大片的狐尾草、灌木叢和雜樹。（夫人喜歡管這叫「灌木刷子」。）你還能望見遠處的大街一角。

column1: You don't say! (Though you certainly try.)
column2: 少來了！（雖然你還真的試著說了。）

column1: That's going to stay right where it's painted.
column2: 這東西畫在哪裡，就會一直留在哪裡。

column1: Sadie Ovaree would probably not appreciate you digging up her carefully cultivated dirt.
column2: 莎蒂·歐薇莉大概不會樂見你挖掘她精心整理過的泥土地。

column1: You can see a corner of the old Engineer's Shack from here.
column2: 你從這裡可以看到老工程師小屋的一角。

column1: There's nothing in the Engineer's Shack worth toying with.
column2: 工程師小屋裡沒什麼值得你亂碰的東西。
